sample_unit: real WESAD stress windows (Phase 2 sensor-loss test)

links.outcome: Stress recall under progressive sensor/feature-modality loss
links.effect: Stress recall fell from 99.58% (CI 98.48-99.88%) on pristine inputs to 95.79% (CI 93.59-97.26%) only after removal of three of five modalities; graceful degradation.
links.quote: Phase 2 showed graceful degradation under progressive sensor loss on 475 real WESAD stress windows, with stress recall declining from 99.58% (95% Wilson CI: [98.48%, 99.88%]) on pristine inputs to 95.79% ([93.59%, 97.26%]) only after simultaneous removal of three of five feature modalities.

links.outcome: Serving-layer completion rate under 50-worker burst load
links.effect: 86.8% completion rate under 50-worker burst load; serving layer identified as the concurrency bottleneck. Mean sequential latency 80.47 ms (p95 84.86 ms).
links.quote: Phase 1 measured a mean sequential HTTP latency of 80.47 milliseconds (ms) (95th percentile [p95] = 84.86 ms), isolated route-level timing across the Machine Learning (ML)-only, Deep Learning (DL)-only, and hybrid paths, and exposed an 86.8% completion rate under 50-worker burst load, thereby identifying the serving layer as the current concurrency bottleneck.

unlisted_practices: Route-level latency and concurrency load testing of the model-serving layer
